leftEvidence.title: Pursuit reaches the prophets at Naioth

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David reports to Samuel; repeated messengers and finally Saul prophesy when they come toward Naioth.
points.right: David asks what he has done, Jonathan promises to learn Saul’s purpose, and a field signal is arranged beside renewed covenant language.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Saul’s pursuit stalls inside prophetic speech inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places covenant loyalty is placed under the threat from Jonathan’s father inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 19:18–24 and 1 Samuel 20:1–23 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Battle, Fame, and Saul’s House” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: David and Jonathan test Saul’s intent

payload.tension: 1 Samuel 19:18–24 foregrounds Saul’s pursuit stalls inside prophetic speech; 1 Samuel 20:1–23 foregrounds covenant loyalty is placed under the threat from Jonathan’s father. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
